So I can buy pants at store X, Y, or Z. Now say I have a baseline that I'm willing to already expend on pants and it will be spent regardless on pants so much so that I consider the money spent and I'm already a new pants owner.

Now store X has basic pants of equal quality and brand to Y and Z, but Y offers some additional pattern work that offers no extra features, but I find this visually appealing to my style, but costs $6 more than X.

Then there's Z who offers a random chance at various styles, but it's a lottery as to which style I get, but it costs $3 dollars more, but I find some of the chance styling more appealing than Y.

So say I have that extra $6 to spend on pants and I consider my options. I can get basic pants, which are just as good as the other brands or I can buy a specific style I like for $6 or take a chance on a style I like even more for $3.

The base question is does this matter to anybody other than me? It's my money, I earned it, and my soon to be pants. So what issue is it that I spend the extra $6 on a specific style I like or $3 on a chance of one I like more? And why is it wrong of a company to make these and offer these, even when I know I reality all of these pants are made by the same company, but ones a big box shop, ones a boutique, and the other is the Loot Crate of pants?

It doesn't matter to anyone else and it should be appreciated that instead of all of us living with the same old stock pants we get choices, because choices are fun.
